segmenti.tekst: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره

ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا ومن سيئات أعمالنا، من يهده الله فلا مضل له ومن يضلل فلا هادي له، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله، أرسله الله بالحق بشيرا ونذيرا وسراجا منيرا، لينذر من كان حيا ويحق القول على الكافرين، صلى الله تعالى عليه وعلى آله الطيبين الطاهرين وأصحابه الكرام الهداة المهتدين وسلم تسليما كثيرا إلى يوم الدين.

قال الله في كتابه الكريم: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ. Praise belongs to the One, Exalted Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala (glorified and exalted is He), Lord of all the worlds, Lord of the Day of Judgment, Lord of jinn and mankind. May blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), upon his family, upon his companions, and upon all those who follow the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.
Respected congregation, in the hutba (Friday sermon) before last we spoke about the deeds that lead a person into Jannah (Paradise) – that is, whoever does them, Allah will admit him into Jannah.
Because of their greatness and importance for the individual and society, so that we may be better believers, better mu'mins, so that we may be better members of the community.
Among those deeds that lead a person into Jannah, my dear brothers, is kindness to parents. Kindness to parents.

It is narrated that a companion named Jahimah came to the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, to consult him, as he wanted to go to battle. What did the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say to him? He said: “Hal laka min umm?” He said: “[unclear]” He said: “I do, O Messenger of Allah.” What did the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say to him: “Ilzamha, fa inna al-jannata 'inda rijlayha” – he said: “Stay with her, for Jannah is at her feet.”

That is, kindness to her will admit you into Jannah, kindness to her will admit you into Jannah. It is also narrated that a man came to the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, and asked him: “Who has the most right to my kindness, to my companionship?” What did he say to him? “Your mother.” He said: “Who after that, O Messenger of Allah?” He said: “Your mother.”

“Then who after that?” He said: “Your mother.” Three times the mother. Then he said: “Who after that, O Messenger of Allah?” He said: “Your father. Your father.” Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says… He mentions in the Qur'an that our mother carries us in weakness upon weakness.

She is weak during pregnancy, and she is weak after pregnancy, then she feeds you, and so on and so forth. That is why the mother – how many sleepless nights… But a person must by no means forget the father, the hero of his children.

Have you not read Surah Yusuf? What does Yusuf, alayhis-salam, say? “إِذْ قَالَ يُوسُفُ لِأَبِيهِ يَا أَبَتِ إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًا وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي سَاجِدِينَ” – “O my dear father, I saw in a dream
eleven stars, the Sun and the Moon prostrating to me.” And what did Ya'qub, his father, say to him? “Qala ya bunayya la taqsus ru'yaka 'ala ikhwatika fa yakidu laka kayda.”
He said: “O my dear little son,” he said, “do not tell these dreams, or what you have dreamed, to your brothers, lest they set you up

or plot some deception [unclear].” That is what fathers are, dear brothers. Why did Yusuf, alayhis-salam, not go to his mother? And why is the mother not mentioned? Because a mother always says: “Oh no, my son, they are your brothers,” and so on and so on.
But the father is firm. Every child knows what his state is. Every child knows. And believe me, dear brothers, as long as the father is alive, a person feels that he is [unclear].

He feels that he is still a child. When the father passes away, that emptiness is felt in the house. As long as the father is alive, a person feels different. And the father is the only person, the only person who wants you to be better than him. We are all brothers, both your own blood brothers and us – when it comes to whether you are better than me or not, everyone will tell you: “Thank you, brother, thank you, well done, but I want to be better than you.” Only your father.
Why? Because your success is his success too. What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say in the Qur'an? Allah has commanded you not to worship anyone other than Him.

“Wa bil-walidayni ihsana” – and to treat your parents well. “Imma yablughanna 'indaka al-kibara ahaduhuma aw kilahuma fala taqul lahuma uffin.” If your parents reach old age with you, or one of the parents, do not say to them even “uff”.
And He says: do not repel them from you, do not drive them away from you. What do we do today, dear brothers? Wallahi, it is sad when one hears that someone's parent is in a nursing home.

That someone's parent is in a nursing home. While he has spread himself out at home with his children, his wife, enjoying himself. And his parent is in a nursing home. Or we have built some little rooms for our parents next to the main house, with some toilet there, [unclear] the parents have their own room, as if they were pets and not parents. As if they were pets and not parents. So that, Allah forbid, they don't say something to his wife, or to our wives, so that they don't offend them somehow. Now, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says:

[unclear], He says: “Wa qul lahuma qawlan karima” – and address them kindly, with beautiful speech. “Wakhfid lahuma janaha adh-dhulli min ar-rahmah” – and, He says, be humble toward them and merciful. “Wa qul Rabbirhamhuma kama rabbayani saghira” – and say: “My Lord, have mercy on them as they had mercy on us when we were small.” How our parents, dear brothers, had mercy on us when we were small.

How many times we fell asleep on our fathers' chests. And now, when we have grown up, become big, we do not see them. We do not see our fathers. We do not see what they tell us. And they are our heroes. Wallahi, they are our heroes.

A father's advice is not like the advice of someone else. Never. In first place is his advice, then ten empty places, then someone else's advice. That is how we should treat our fathers and our mothers.

What does the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say? He said: “He is ruined, he is ruined, he is ruined,” three times. They said: “Who, O Messenger of Allah?” He said: “The one who lives to see his parents' old age, or one of his parents', and what?
and does not earn Jannah through kindness to them.” How Islam, dear brothers, teaches us only what is beautiful, nothing else. Islam leads you only to what is beautiful.

And what we hear from the media… Unfortunately, today we Muslims learn about Islam from the media. We do not learn about Islam from books, from recognized scholars, but from the media that feed us all sorts of things.

But this is the beauty of Islam. Islam is beautiful, a very beautiful and practical, and practical religion. The second thing the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, mentions, which will lead a person into Jannah, he says: removing from the road something that harms people.
That a person removes from the road something that harms people. What does the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say? He said: “I saw a man in Jannah turning about.” What, turning about?

Turning from shade to shade, enjoying the blessings of Jannah. Enjoying the blessings of Jannah. “What did he do, O Messenger of Allah?” He said: “He moved a tree, or removed a tree from the road, that was harming people.”
What do we do today? Snow falls. A person, in order to clear his yard, throws or dumps the snow in the middle of the street. What kind of behavior is that? What kind of arrogance is that?

A person digs the foundation of a house. What does he do? He dumps the earth on the road. Or beside the road, so that no one can park, [unclear]. We want to renovate something – all that rubbish goes into nature.
But Islam teaches us the opposite, and we see, dear brothers, what the reward is. Unfortunately, we call our fellow citizens who clean the streets every day “garbage men”.

Unfortunately… they are not the garbage men; rather, those who throw garbage on the road, in nature, in the rivers – they are the real garbage men. And these people who collect garbage and clean our city, they are gentlemen.

They are, in fact, gentlemen. Today, if you picked something up to remove it from the road, Allah forbid, or to clean something up, people would mock you. They would say: [unclear], he's gone mad, he's lost his mind, and so on.

But in fact such a person is only practicing the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, and if he hopes for Allah's reward, Allah will give him the reward, and that is Jannah. The next thing the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, mentions is performing voluntary prayers, or nafl prayers. Rabi'ah ibn Ka'b said: “O Messenger of Allah, I would love to be beside you in Jannah.” What did the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say to him? He said: “Increase the number of your prostrations.”

That is, make many prostrations to Allah, many voluntary prayers. What do we do today? Today, as soon as the fard (obligatory) prayer is over, we leave straight from the fard. [unclear] two or three men remain there to pray the sunnah with us. He arrives exactly for the fard and leaves straight after the fard.

No dhikr, no sunnah, nothing. That is why Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala… these deeds are easy. Easy at first glance. But for some people they are hard. Here we are talking about those who pray the sunnah prayers; and those who do not pray at all, neither the fard nor the sunnah –
those people are a separate story, and a separate story is for them. This is not a story for them. This is a story for those who pray the fard but do not pray the sunnah or voluntary prayers.

So whoever makes as many prostrations to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, as possible, Allah promises him Jannah through His Messenger. The next thing for which the Prophet promises us Jannah is good character.

The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: the people I love most among you are the people – of what? – of the best character, the most beautiful character. And they will be beside me – where, dear brothers? In Jannah. Closest to me in Jannah.

This is a great incentive, and an incentive for people to send their children to the mekteb (Qur'an school), dear brothers. To guide their children and bring them up properly. Because when a person is 20 years old, 25 years old, you cannot bring him up.

Except the one upon whom Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, has mercy. It saddens me when a man comes and says: “I can't [unclear],” he says, “my son of 11–12 years.” You can't? But he lives on your money. He sleeps in your house.

“I can't,” he says, “forbid my daughter from going out. My daughter is 14–15 years old.” Well, my brother, she goes out on your money, she goes into town half-naked. She doesn't go on my money. You can prevent it if you want. That is why a person should raise a child while he is small.

From his early years. To send him to the mekteb, to bring him up, to take him along with him. What do people do today? They won't take their son along with them. They say: “Let him be, he's with his friends.” But a child learns best when he is with older people, at a gathering, over coffee.

He takes his son along, and that way he learns from the elders how to behave, how to be a man. If he always takes him or lets him go with his friends, he has nothing to learn from them. They are on the same level, and then the child stagnates, stands still.

Also, among the things for which the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, promises us Jannah is, is whoever takes care of an orphan. What does the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say? He said: “I and the one who takes care of orphans, of an orphan, will be in Jannah,” he said, “like these two,” he said, “fingers” – like this, close.

Why, dear brothers, such a great reward? First, because that orphan has no parents, has no one to take care of him. And you have taken it upon yourself to take care of that orphan and you love him as you love your own children.

And you buy for him as you buy for your own children. And that is hard. And that is hard, by Allah. It is easy only for the one upon whom Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, has mercy. What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say? “Wa la ta'kulu amwalahum ila amwalikum.”
And He says: do not, He says, take their money and spend it, that is, put it together with your own money. There are people – he takes care of an orphan, and the orphan has some money,

and he mixes that orphan's money with his own money and then spends it. That, dear brothers, is not right; rather, you should guard his money and not spend it except when there is a really great need.

These are all things, dear brothers, to which Islam calls us, things that are truly beautiful. Things that are beautiful, that are beneficial for the community and for society. So whoever does them will have Jannah from Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.
I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to forgive us our sins and the sins of our parents. I ask Him, the Exalted, to admit us into Jannah. Amin.
